SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsContinua.d: Liability for extension of life insurance coverage in instances where coverage under the plan would otherwise end.

SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsDisabili.l: Supplemental Unemployment Benefits, Disability Related Benefits
SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsDisabili.d: Liability for amount due a former employee for benefits as a result of them becoming physically or mentally impaired.

SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsJobTrain.l: Supplemental Unemployment Benefits, Job Training and Counseling
SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsJobTrain.d: Liability for benefits that provide the former employee with career counseling assistance and instruction in learning new skills, to assist them in finding another source of employment.

SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsOtherPos.d: Amount of postemployment benefit liabilities classified as other.

SupplementalUnemploymentBenefitsSeveranc.d: Liability for amount due employees, in addition to wages and any other money that employers owe employees, when their employment ends through a layoff or other termination. For example, a company may provide involuntarily terminated employees with a lump sum payment equal to one week's salary for every year of employment.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationAmortiz.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Amortization of Deferred Policy Acquisition Cost
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationAmortiz.d: Amount of amortization of deferred policy acquisition cost recognized, as disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationBenefit.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Benefit, Claim, Loss and Settlement Expenses
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationBenefit.d: Amount of insurance benefit, claim, loss and settlement expenses incurred, as disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationDeferre.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Deferred Policy Acquisition Cost
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationDeferre.d: Amount of deferred policy acquisition cost capitalized on contract remaining in force, as disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationLiabili.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Liability for Future Policy Benefit, Loss, Claim and Loss Expense
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationLiabili.d: Amount of reserve for future policy claim payable and loss expense to be incurred, disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationNetInve.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Net Investment Income
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationNetInve.d: Amount of net investment income earned, disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationOtherOp.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Other Operating Expense
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationOtherOp.d: Amount of operating expense classified as other, disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationOtherPo.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Other Policy Claim and Benefit Payable
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationOtherPo.d: Amount of claim and benefit payable classified as other, disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationPremium.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Premium Revenue
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationPremium.d: Amount of premium revenue earned, disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplementaryInsuranceInformationPremium.l: SEC Schedule, 12-16, Insurance Companies, Supplementary Insurance Information, Premium Written
SupplementaryInsuranceInformationPremium.d: Amount, after premiums ceded and assumed, of premium written, disclosed in supplementary insurance information.

SupplierConcentrationRiskMember.d: Reflects the percentage that purchases in the period from one or more significant suppliers is to cost of goods or services, as defined by the entity, such as total cost of sales or services, product line cost of sales or services, segment cost of sales or services. Risk is the materially adverse effects of loss of a material supplier or a supplier of critically needed goods or services.

Supplies.d: Amount of consideration paid in advance for supplies that provide economic benefits within a future period of one year or the normal operating cycle, if longer.

SwapMember.d: A forward-based contract in which two parties agree to swap streams of payments over a specified period. The payment streams are based on an agreed-upon (or notional) principal amount. The term notional is used because swap contracts generally involve no exchange of principal at either inception or maturity. Rather, the notional amount serves as a basis for calculation of the payment streams to be exchanged.

SwaptionMember.d: Option contract giving the holder the right to enter into a swap.

TangibleCapital.d: Amount of tangible capital as defined by regulatory framework.

TangibleCapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequac.d: Amount of minimum tangible capital required for capital adequacy as defined by regulatory framework.

TargetedOrTrackingStockDescriptionTextBl.l: Targeted or Tracking Stock [Table Text Block]
TargetedOrTrackingStockDescriptionTextBl.d: Tabular disclosure of quantitative and qualitative information related to target or tracking stock issued, including, but not limited to, pricing of transactions and cost allocation method used.

TaxCreditCarryforwardAmount.d: The amount of the tax credit carryforward, before tax effects, available to reduce future taxable income under enacted tax laws.

TaxCreditCarryforwardNameDomain.d: The name of the tax credit carryforward.

TaxCreditCarryforwardLimitationsOnUse.l: Tax Credit Carryforward, Limitations on Use
TaxCreditCarryforwardLimitationsOnUse.d: Description of the limitation related to use of the tax credit carryforward.

TaxCreditCarryforwardValuationAllowance.d: Amount of valuation allowance pertaining to the deferred tax asset representing potential future taxable deductions from tax credit carryforwards for which it is more likely than not that a tax benefit will not be realized.

TaxCreditCarryforwardAxis.d: Information by specific tax credit related to an unused tax credit.

TaxCreditCarryforwardLineItems.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

TaxCreditCarryforwardTable.d: Disclosure of information about tax credit carryforward available to reduce future taxable income. Includes, but is not limited to, description, amount, expiration date, limitation on use, and related deferred tax asset and valuation allowance.

IncomeTaxesPaid.l: Income Tax Paid, before Refund Received
IncomeTaxesPaid.d: Amount, before refund, of cash paid to foreign, federal, state, and local jurisdictions as income tax.

TechnologyEquipmentMember.d: Equipment used in the creation, maintenance and utilization of information systems which include computers and peripherals.

ContractTerminationClaimsDescription.d: General description of claims, deemed to be reimbursable and included in accounts receivable, relating to the termination of long-term government contracts and programs. Includes claims associated with terminated war and defense contracts. If a reasonable estimate of a termination claim is undeterminable or impossible to make, disclosure is made to discuss the status and circumstances related to the undeterminable claim.

ContractTerminationClaimsGovernmentsOthe.l: Contract Termination Claims, Governments Other than US Federal Government
ContractTerminationClaimsGovernmentsOthe.d: Amount included in accounts receivable for long-term contracts and programs associated with governmental contracts at the balance sheet date representing amounts deemed to be reimbursable items under a terminated government contract or subcontract and included in a claim with a customer other than United States federal government.

ContractTerminationClaimsUSFederalGovern.l: Contract Termination Claims, US Federal Government
ContractTerminationClaimsUSFederalGovern.d: Amount included in accounts receivable for long-term contracts and programs associated with governmental contracts at the balance sheet date representing amounts deemed to be reimbursable items under a terminated United States government contract or subcontract and included in a claim with the United States government, including those associated with terminated war and defense contracts.

TerminationLoans.d: Definite liabilities to third parties under a termination loan agreement, whether or not guaranteed in whole or in part by the government.

TerminationLoansDescription.d: General description of liabilities to third parties under a termination loan agreement, whether or not guaranteed by the government, including a cross reference to the related termination claim or claims recorded or disclosed at the latest balance sheet date.

ThreatOfExpropriationOfAssetsMember.d: The risk of loss pertaining to the potential threat that a political body may take away certain assets of the company without fair, and possibly with little or no, compensation.

TierOneLeverageCapital.l: Banking Regulation, Tier 1 Leverage Capital, Actual
TierOneLeverageCapital.d: Amount of Tier 1 leverage capital as defined by regulatory framework.

TierOneLeverageCapitalRequiredForCapital.l: Banking Regulation, Tier 1 Leverage Capital, Capital Adequacy, Minimum
TierOneLeverageCapitalRequiredForCapital.d: Amount of minimum Tier 1 leverage capital required for capital adequacy as defined by regulatory framework.

TierOneLeverageCapitalRequiredToBeWellCa.l: Banking Regulation, Tier 1 Leverage Capital, Well Capitalized, Minimum
TierOneLeverageCapitalRequiredToBeWellCa.d: Amount of minimum Tier 1 leverage capital categorized as well capitalized as defined by regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.

TierOneRiskBasedCapital.l: Banking Regulation, Tier 1 Risk-Based Capital, Actual
TierOneRiskBasedCapital.d: Amount of Tier 1 risk-based capital as defined by regulatory framework.

TierOneRiskBasedCapitalRequiredForCapita.l: Banking Regulation, Tier 1 Risk-Based Capital, Capital Adequacy, Minimum
TierOneRiskBasedCapitalRequiredForCapita.d: Amount of minimum Tier 1 risk-based capital required for capital adequacy as defined by regulatory framework.

TierOneRiskBasedCapitalRequiredToBeWellC.l: Banking Regulation, Tier 1 Risk-Based Capital, Well Capitalized, Minimum
TierOneRiskBasedCapitalRequiredToBeWellC.d: Amount of minimum Tier 1 risk-based capital categorized as well capitalized as defined by regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.

TimberPropertiesMember.d: Land devoted primarily to the growth and harvest of forest crops for commercial purposes.

TimeDepositLiabilitiesDescription.d: Description of time deposits (deposits that do not mature until a specific date and for which there may be penalties for withdrawing prior to maturity) held by the entity, which may include a description of the types and repayment terms of the deposits, the amount of the liabilities recognized for the deposits, the aggregate amount of time deposits (including certificates of deposit) in denominations of less than $100,000, and the aggregate amount of time deposits (including certificates of depo

TimeDepositMaturitiesAfterYearFive.l: Time Deposit Maturities, after Year Five
TimeDepositMaturitiesAfterYearFive.d: Amount of time deposit maturing after fifth fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

TimeDepositMaturitiesYearFive.d: Amount of time deposit maturing in fifth fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

TimeDepositMaturitiesYearFour.d: Amount of time deposit maturing in fourth fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

TimeDepositMaturitiesYearOne.d: Amount of time deposit maturing in next fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

TimeDepositMaturitiesYearThree.d: Amount of time deposit maturing in third fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

TimeDepositMaturitiesYearTwo.d: Amount of time deposit maturing in second fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

TimeDeposits100000OrMore.d: Amount of time deposit liabilities, including certificates of deposit, in denominations of $100,000 or more.

BankTimeDepositsMember.d: Certificates of deposit (CD) or savings accounts with a fixed term or understanding the customer can only withdraw by giving advanced notice with a bank or other financial institution. A CD is a short to medium-term investment available at banks and savings and loan institutions where a customer agrees to lend money to the institution for a certain amount of time and is paid a predetermined rate of interest.

TimeDepositsNoncurrent.l: Time Deposit Maturities, after Year One
TimeDepositsNoncurrent.d: Amount of time deposit maturing after next fiscal year following current fiscal year. Time deposit includes, but is not limited to, certificate of deposit. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach).

ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.l: Contractual Maturities, Time Deposits, $100,000 or More, after 12 Months
ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.d: Amount of time deposit liabilities, including certificates of deposit, in denominations of $100,000 or more, maturing after twelve months from the balance sheet date.

ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.l: Contractual Maturities, Time Deposits, $100,000 or More, 6 Months through 12 Months
ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.d: Amount of time deposit liabilities, including certificates of deposit, in denominations of $100,000 or more, maturing within six to twelve months after the balance sheet date.

ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.l: Contractual Maturities, Time Deposits, $100,000 or More, Three Months or Less
ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.d: Amount of time deposit liabilities, including certificates of deposit, in denominations of $100,000 or more, maturing within three months or fewer from the balance sheet date.

ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.l: Contractual Maturities, Time Deposits, $100,000 or More, Three Months Through Six Months
ContractualMaturitiesTimeDeposits100000O.d: Amount of time deposit liabilities, including certificates of deposit, in denominations of $100,000 or more, maturing within three to six months after the balance sheet date.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Greater than Five Years
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities greater than five years.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Greater than One Year
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities greater than one year.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Year Five
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities greater than four years, but five years or less.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Year Four
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities greater than three years, but four years or less.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Year One
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities of one year or less.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Year Three
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities greater than two years, but three years or less.

TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.l: Time Deposits, Weighted Average Interest Rate, Maturities Year Two
TimeDepositsWeightedAverageInterestRateM.d: Weighted average interest rate for time deposits held by the entity with maturities greater than one year, but two years or less.

InventoryRealEstateTimeshareAvailableFor.d: Amount of real estate which is available for sale in the form of shared property ownership in which rights vest in several owners (buyers, timeshare holders) to use the property for a specified period each year (timeshare). Included in this item would be real estate assets in which timeshares are for sale, such as in condominiums at timeshare resorts. Excluded from this item would be assets, other than real estate, in which the Entity has sold or intends to sell timeshares, such as for cruises,

LiabilityForTitleClaimsAndClaimsAdjustme.l: Liability for Title Claims and Claims Adjustment Expense (Deprecated 2024)
LiabilityForTitleClaimsAndClaimsAdjustme.d: The amount needed to reflect the estimated ultimate cost of settling asserted and unasserted claims estimated to have been incurred by the insureds on or before the balance sheet date pertaining to the existence of a lien, encumbrance, defect or other matter purportedly affecting the title to the interest as insured.

TitleInsuranceSegmentMember.d: Contract providing insurance coverage against loss of interest in property due to legal defect.

ToolsDiesAndMoldsMember.d: Equipment commonly used to cut, shape, and form metal and other materials into goods for sale.

TornadoMember.d: Localized violently destructive windstorm characterized by a funnel shaped cloud.

RealEstateAssetsHeldForDevelopmentAndSal.l: Real Estate Assets Held for Development and Sale
RealEstateAssetsHeldForDevelopmentAndSal.d: For banks, the total amount of real estate assets held for development and sale.

Capital.d: Amount of total capital as defined by regulatory framework.

CapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequacy.l: Banking Regulation, Total Risk-Based Capital, Capital Adequacy, Minimum
CapitalRequiredForCapitalAdequacy.d: Amount of minimum total risk-based capital required for capital adequacy as defined by regulatory framework.

CapitalRequiredToBeWellCapitalized.l: Banking Regulation, Total Risk-Based Capital, Well Capitalized, Minimum
CapitalRequiredToBeWellCapitalized.d: Amount of minimum total risk-based capital categorized as well capitalized as defined by regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.

AssetsCurrent.d: Amount of asset recognized for present right to economic benefit, classified as current.

RealEstateLiabilitiesAssociatedWithAsset.l: Real Estate Liabilities Associated with Assets Held for Development and Sale
RealEstateLiabilitiesAssociatedWithAsset.d: For banks, amount of all liabilities for which a financial institution is required to include in its calculation of net investment in real estate assets held for development or sale.

NoninterestExpense.d: Total aggregate amount of all noninterest expense.

RevenuesExcludingInterestAndDividends.d: Revenues from operations, excluding interest and dividend income. Includes revenues from the following sources: investment banking (underwriting and financial advisory), principal transactions (sales and trading, and investment gains and losses), commissions, asset management, and investment advisory and other services.

AccountsReceivableGrossCurrent.l: Accounts Receivable, before Allowance for Credit Loss, Current
AccountsReceivableGrossCurrent.d: Amount, before allowance for credit loss, of right to consideration from customer for product sold and service rendered in normal course of business, classified as current.

TradeNamesMember.d: Rights acquired through registration of a business name to gain or protect exclusive use thereof.

TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleAmount.d: Amount, before valuation allowance, of accounts receivable held for sale.

TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleNetReconcilia.l: Accounts Receivable, Held-for-Sale, Not Part of Disposal Group, after Valuation Allowance, Reconciliation to Cash Flow [Roll Forward]
TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleNetReconcilia.d: A roll forward is a reconciliation of a concept from the beginning of a period to the end of a period.

TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleReconciliatio.l: Accounts Receivable, Held-for-Sale, Not Part of Disposal Group, Reconciliation to Cash Flow, Addition to Held-for-Sale
TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleReconciliatio.d: Amount, after allowance for credit loss, of addition to trade receivable held for sale that is not part of disposal group.

TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleReconciliatio.l: Accounts Receivable, Held-for-Sale, Not Part of Disposal Group, Reconciliation to Cash Flow, Period Increase (Decrease)
TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleReconciliatio.d: Amount, after allowance for credit loss, of increase (decrease) in trade receivable held for sale that is not part of disposal group.

TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleReconciliatio.l: Accounts Receivable, Held-for-Sale, Not Part of Disposal Group, Reconciliation to Cash Flow, Deduction from Held-for-Sale
TradeReceivablesHeldForSaleReconciliatio.d: Amount, after allowance for credit loss, of deduction to trade receivable held for sale that is not part of disposal group.

TradeSecretsMember.d: Information generally known to only a limited number of the entity's employees, such as a formula, pattern, machine, technology, and production process that may give an entity a competitive advantage.

TrademarksMember.d: Rights acquired through registration of a trademark to gain or protect exclusive use of a business name, symbol or other device or style.

TradingGainsLosses.d: Amount of gain (loss) resulting from the difference between the acquisition price and the selling price or fair value of trading assets and trading liabilities, conducted separately from customer trading activities. Includes, but is not limited to, changes in fair value of trading assets and trading liabilities.

TradingLiabilities.d: The carrying amount of liabilities as of the balance sheet date that pertain to principal and customer trading transactions, or which may be incurred with the objective of generating a profit from short-term fluctuations in price as part of an entity's market-making, hedging and proprietary trading. Examples include short positions in securities, derivatives and commodities, obligations under repurchase agreements, and securities borrowed arrangements.

TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsAb.l: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets [Abstract]

TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsPo.l: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets, Policy [Policy Text Block]
TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsPo.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for transfers and servicing financial assets, including securitization transactions as well as repurchase and resale agreements. This disclosure may include how the entity (1) determines whether a transaction is accounted for as a sale; (2) accounts for a sale transaction, including the initial and subsequent accounting for any interests that the entity obtains or continues to hold in the transaction, how such interests are valued, and the significant assumptions

TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsSe.l: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets, Servicing of Financial Assets, Policy [Policy Text Block]
TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsSe.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for servicing assets and liabilities including, but not necessarily limited to: (a) how a servicing asset or servicing liability is initially recognized and measured, (b) management's basis for determining its classes of servicing assets and servicing liabilities, (c) where contractually specified fees, late fees or ancillary fees are reported in the statement of income, (d) how the entity subsequently measures each class of servicing assets and servicing liabilit

TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTr.l: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets, Transfers of Financial Assets, Policy [Policy Text Block]
TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTr.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for transfers of financial assets, including securitization transactions. The disclosure is generally expected to include how the entity determines whether a transaction is accounted for as a sale or financing, and the initial and subsequent accounting for such a transaction. The disclosure also may address how interests that are obtained and sold, or those that continue to be held, in such transactions are measured and accounted for, and the methodology and signi

TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTr.l: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets, Transfers of Financial Assets, Financings, Policy [Policy Text Block]
TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTr.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for recognizing whether a transfer of a financial asset is accounted for as a financing, and its initial and subsequent accounting for such a transaction.

TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTr.l: Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets, Transfers of Financial Assets, Sales, Policy [Policy Text Block]
TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTr.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for recognizing whether a transfer of a financial asset qualifies for sale treatment, and its initial and subsequent accounting for a sale transaction. If an entity has securitized financial assets during any period presented and accounts for that transfer as a sale, for each major asset type (for example, mortgage loans, credit card receivables, and automobile loans), the entity generally discloses its accounting policies for initially and subsequently measuring

LongTermTransitionBond.d: Long-Term transition bonds are bonds under the Competition Act in which the proceeds of Transition Bonds are required to be used principally to reduce qualified stranded costs and the related capitalization of the utility. This represents the noncurrent portion.

TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.l: Derivatives used in Net Investment Hedge, Net of Tax [Roll Forward]
TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.d: A roll forward is a reconciliation of a concept from the beginning of a period to the end of a period.

TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.l: Derivatives used in Net Investment Hedge, Increase (Decrease), Gross of Tax
TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.d: Amount, before tax, of increase (decrease) in the cumulative translation adjustment from gain (loss) on foreign currency derivatives that are designated as, and are effective as, economic hedges of a net investment in a foreign entity.

TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.l: Derivatives used in Net Investment Hedge, Net of Tax, Period Increase (Decrease)
TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.d: Amount of increase (decrease) in the cumulative translation adjustment from gain (loss), after tax, on foreign currency derivatives, that are designated as, and are effective as, economic hedges of a net investment in a foreign entity.

TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.l: Gain (Loss) on Derivative Used in Net Investment Hedge, after Tax
TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.d: Amount, after tax, of reclassification from accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) of gain (loss) from increase (decrease) in fair value of net investment hedge.

TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.l: Derivatives used in Net Investment Hedge, Net of Tax
TranslationAdjustmentForNetInvestmentHed.d: Amount, after tax, of cumulative translation adjustment attributable to gain (loss) on foreign currency derivatives that are designated as, and are effective as, economic hedges of a net investment in a foreign entity.

TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.l: Translation Adjustment Functional to Reporting Currency [Roll Forward]
TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.d: A roll forward is a reconciliation of a concept from the beginning of a period to the end of a period.

TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.l: Translation Adjustment Functional to Reporting Currency, Increase (Decrease), Gross of Tax
TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.d: Amount of cumulative translation gain (loss), before tax, from translating foreign currency financial statements into the reporting currency.

TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.l: Translation Adjustment Functional to Reporting Currency, Net of Tax, Period Increase (Decrease)
TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.d: Amount of increase (decrease) in cumulative translation adjustment, after tax, from translating foreign currency financial statements into the reporting currency.

TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.l: Translation Adjustment Functional to Reporting Currency, Net of Tax
TranslationAdjustmentFunctionalToReporti.d: Amount of cumulative translation gain (loss), after tax, from translating foreign currency financial statements into the reporting currency.

IndependentTransmissionAndDistributionSy.d: System for the transmission and distribution of electricity, gas, water, or other fuels and materials.

TransportationAdvanceTicketArrangementMe.d: Category of deferred revenue by arrangement wherein advance air, sea and land transportation tickets issued to customers are recognized as revenue when transportation service is provided.

TransportationEquipmentMember.d: Equipment used for the primary purpose of moving people and products from one place to another.

TravelAndEntertainmentExpense.d: Expenses incurred for travel and entertainment during the period.

TreasuryStockNumberOfSharesAndRestrictio.l: Treasury Stock, Number of Shares and Restriction Disclosures [Abstract]

TreasuryStockAcquiredAverageCostPerShare.l: Shares Acquired, Average Cost Per Share
TreasuryStockAcquiredAverageCostPerShare.d: Total cost of shares repurchased divided by the total number of shares repurchased.

TreasuryStockAcquiredPurchasePriceSignif.l: Treasury Stock Acquired, Purchase Price Significantly in Excess of Current Fair Value, Description
TreasuryStockAcquiredPurchasePriceSignif.d: Description of accounting treatment for treasury stock acquired at a price significantly in excess of the fair value.

TreasuryStockAcquiredRepurchaseAuthoriza.d: Description of share repurchase program, including accounting treatment.

TreasuryStockSharesRetired.d: Number of shares of common and preferred stock retired from treasury during the period.

StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesTreasurySto.l: Stock Issued During Period, Shares, Treasury Stock Reissued
StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesTreasurySto.d: Number of treasury shares or units reissued. Excludes reissuance of shares or units in treasury for award under share-based payment arrangement.

StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueTreasuryStoc.l: Stock Issued During Period, Value, Treasury Stock Reissued
StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueTreasuryStoc.d: Value of treasury shares or units reissued. Excludes reissuance of shares or units in treasury for award under share-based payment arrangement.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period, Description of Changes in Terms
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: For a debtor, a description of the changes in terms of an existing debt, the major features of settlement, or both. This could include transferring to the creditor receivables from third parties, granting of equity interest in the debtor to the creditor, or modifying terms of the debt.

GainsLossesOnRestructuringOfDebt.d: For a debtor, the aggregate gain (loss) recognized on the restructuring of payables arises from the difference between the book value of the debt before the restructuring and the fair value of the payments on the debt after restructuring is complete.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period, Gain (Loss) on Restructuring, Net of Tax
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: For a debtor, the aggregate gain (loss) recognized on the restructuring of payables, after the impact of income tax expense or benefit, arising from the difference between the book value of the debt before the restructuring and the fair value of the payments on the debt after restructuring is complete.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period, Gain (Loss) on Restructuring, Tax Effect
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: Amount of income tax expense (benefit) on the gain (loss) recognized for the restructuring of payables for troubled debt restructurings.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period [Abstract]
Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period, Creditor [Domain]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: For a debtor, the name of the Creditor with whom the terms are being restructured.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period, Gain (Loss) on Restructuring, Per Share, Net
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: Provide the per share amount of gain (loss), after the impact of income taxes, on restructuring of payables (or debt) for all restructuring gains (losses) (in aggregate) during the period.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period [Line Items]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Current Period [Table]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorCurrentPe.d: Disclosure of information about debtor's troubled debt restructuring in period restructured.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorOther.d: Voluntary or miscellaneous disclosures regarding a troubled debt restructuring, not otherwise listed in the existing taxonomy.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Subsequent Periods, Contingent Payments, Amount
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.d: Amount of restructured debt contingently payable based on the occurrence of future events or circumstances.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Subsequent Periods, Contingent Payments, Conditions
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.d: For a debtor, a description of the circumstance, events, or conditions that would cause payments to occur or the creditor to forgive the contingent portion of recorded debt.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Subsequent Periods, Contingent Payments, Name [Domain]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.d: Name of the troubled debt restructuring.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Subsequent Periods [Axis]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.d: Information by category of troubled debt restructuring.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Subsequent Periods [Line Items]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.l: Troubled Debt Restructuring, Debtor, Subsequent Period [Table]
TroubledDebtRestructuringDebtorSubsequen.d: Disclosure of information about debtor's troubled debt restructuring subsequent to period restructured.

TrustPreferredSecuritiesSubjectToMandato.l: Trust Preferred Securities Subject to Mandatory Redemption [Member]
TrustPreferredSecuritiesSubjectToMandato.d: Preferred securities that embody an unconditional obligation requiring the issuer to redeem the securities by transferring the assets at a specified or determinable date (or dates) or upon an event that is certain to occur, that are issued by a consolidated trust to outside investors where the trust uses the proceeds of the issuance of those securities to purchase, from the financial institution that established the trust, an equivalent amount of junior subordinated debentures or other loans hav

TrusteeFees.d: Fees charged annually for the professional services of a trustee, usually quoted as a percentage of the funds being managed. The fee for appointing an offshore Trustee is included in the trust price.

TsunamiMember.d: Cataclysm resulting from a destructive sea wave caused by an earthquake or volcanic eruption.

TypesOfItemsHedgedByForeignCurrencyDeriv.l: Types of Items Hedged by Foreign Currency Derivatives (Deprecated 2025)
TypesOfItemsHedgedByForeignCurrencyDeriv.d: Description of hedged items in foreign currency hedges.

TypesOfItemsHedgedByInterestRateDerivati.l: Types of Items Hedged by Interest Rate Derivatives (Deprecated 2025)
TypesOfItemsHedgedByInterestRateDerivati.d: Description of the instruments designated as hedged items in hedges involving interest rate derivatives.

TypesOfItemsHedgedByPriceRiskDerivatives.l: Types of Items Hedged by Price Risk Derivatives (Deprecated 2025)
TypesOfItemsHedgedByPriceRiskDerivatives.d: Description of the instruments designated as hedged items in hedges involving price risk derivatives. For example, a forecasted purchase of commodity inventory or the fair value of equity securities held.

USGovernmentCorporationsAndAgenciesSecur.l: US Government Corporations and Agencies Securities [Member]
USGovernmentCorporationsAndAgenciesSecur.d: This category includes information about debt issued by US Government Corporations and Agencies. Investments in such US Government Corporations may include debt securities issued by the Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) and by the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac).

USGovernmentDebtSecuritiesMember.d: Debt securities issued by the United States government.

USStatesAndPoliticalSubdivisionsMember.l: US States and Political Subdivisions Debt Securities [Member]
USStatesAndPoliticalSubdivisionsMember.d: Bonds or similar securities issued by state, city, or local US governments or the agencies operated by state, city, or local governments. Debt securities issued by state governments may include bond issuances of US state authorities including, for example, but not limited to, housing authorities, dormitory authorities, and general obligations while debt securities issued by political subdivisions of US states would include, for example, debt issuances by county, borough, city, or municipal gover

USTreasuryAndGovernmentMember.d: This category includes investments in debt securities issued by the United States Department of the Treasury, US Government Agencies and US Government-sponsored Enterprises. Such securities may include treasury bills (short-term maturities - one year or less), treasury notes (intermediate term maturities - two to ten years), and treasury bonds (long-term maturities - ten to thirty years), debt securities issued by the Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) and debt securities issu

USTreasurySecuritiesMember.d: This category includes information about debt securities issued by the United States Department of the Treasury and backed by the United States government. Such securities primarily consist of treasury bills (short-term maturities - one year or less), treasury notes (intermediate term maturities - two to ten years), and treasury bonds (long-term maturities - ten to thirty years).

USGovernmentSecuritiesAtCarryingValue.l: Cash Equivalent, US Government Security, Carrying Value
USGovernmentSecuritiesAtCarryingValue.d: Debt (bills, notes or bonds) that are issued by the government of the United States which are short-term, highly liquid investments that are both readily convertible to known amounts of cash and so near their maturity that they present insignificant risk of changes in value because of changes in interest rates. Generally, only investments with original maturities of three months or less qualify under that definition. Original maturity means original maturity to the entity holding the investment.

FinancialInstrumentsSoldNotYetPurchasedU.l: Financial Instruments Sold, Not yet Purchased, US Government and Agency Obligations
FinancialInstrumentsSoldNotYetPurchasedU.d: Fair value of obligations arising from US treasury and other US government and agency debt obligations sold short.

UnamortizedDiscountsOnAcceptancesExecute.d: The amount of the unearned (fee) income on the financial institution's issuance of short-term negotiable time drafts (also known as Banker's Acceptances).

UnamortizedDiscountsOnAcceptancesResold.d: The amount of the unamortized discount or expense related to the financial institution's sale of short-term negotiable time drafts drawn on and accepted by the institution (also known as Banker's Acceptances) in the secondary market.

UnamortizedLossReacquiredDebtNoncurrent.d: Unamortized Loss on Reacquired Debt is the loss incurred upon reacquisition or refinancing of debt, is treated as a deferred charge and amortized over the life of the new debt issued.

UnbilledChangeOrdersAmountExpectedToBeCo.l: Unbilled Change Orders, Amount Expected to be Collected after One Year
UnbilledChangeOrdersAmountExpectedToBeCo.d: Amount of unbilled change orders from customers under long-term contracts or programs associated with unpriced change orders or other similar items subject to uncertainty concerning their determination or ultimate realization which is expected to be collected after one year from the balance sheet date.

UncollectibleReceivablesMember.d: A revision in the estimated reserve needed to reduce the carrying amount of accounts receivable to net realizable value with respect to credit and collection risk.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligations Disclosure [Table Text Block]
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Tabular disclosure of unconditional purchase obligation not recognized as liability.

UnderwritingIncomeLoss.d: The difference between the price paid by the public and the contract price less the related expenses. A broker-dealer may underwrite a security offering by contracting to buy the issue either at a fixed price or a price based on selling the offering on a best-effort basis.

UnionizedEmployeesConcentrationRiskMembe.d: Reflects the percentage that unionized employees, in either labor costs for the period or number of personnel as of the balance sheet date or on average for the period, are to a specified benchmark, such as total operating expenses, total labor costs, total corresponding number of personnel. Risk is the materially adverse effects of strikes and unfavorable contract negotiations with employees covered by collective bargaining arrangements.

UnitDistributionMember.d: Distribution of units made by the entity based on a contractual agreement such as a partnership or employment agreement.

UnitsOfPartnershipInterestAmount.d: The number of units or equivalent units outstanding for all classes.

UnitsOfPartnershipInterestDescription.d: Description of the ownership interests of the partnership which are represented by units. There may be different classes of units which have different preferences and conversion rights to stock or cash. Also includes a discussion of each class of members' interests and respective rights, preferences and privileges.

UniversalLifeMember.d: Life insurance contract under which premiums are generally flexible, the level of death benefits may be adjusted, and mortality expense, and other charges may vary.

LiabilityForUnpaidClaimsAndClaimsAdjustm.l: Liability for Unpaid Claims and Claims Adjustment Expense, Period Increase (Decrease)
LiabilityForUnpaidClaimsAndClaimsAdjustm.d: Amount, after effects of reinsurance, of increase (decrease) in the liability for unpaid claims and claims adjustment expense.

UnpaidPolicyClaimsAndClaimsAdjustmentExp.l: Unpaid Policy Claims and Claims Adjustment Expense, Policy [Policy Text Block]
UnpaidPolicyClaimsAndClaimsAdjustmentExp.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for estimating the ultimate cost of settling insurance claims relating to insured events that have occurred on or before a particular date (ordinarily, the statement of financial position date). The estimated liability includes the amount of money that will be required for future payments of (a) claims that have been reported to the insurer, (b) claims related to insured events that have occurred but that have not been reported to the insurer as of the date the li

UnpatentedTechnologyMember.d: Technology-based innovations or scientific advances that have not been patented.

UnprovedOilAndGasPropertySuccessfulEffor.l: Oil and Gas, Successful Efforts Method, Property and Equipment, Unproved Property, before Accumulated Depreciation, Depletion, Amortization, and Impairment
UnprovedOilAndGasPropertySuccessfulEffor.d: Amount, before accumulated depreciation, depletion, amortization, and impairment, of oil and gas properties with unproved reserve accounted for under successful efforts method.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsDecreasesResultin.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Decrease Resulting from Current Period Tax Positions
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsDecreasesResultin.d: Amount of decrease in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from tax positions that have been or will be taken in current period tax return.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsReductionsResulti.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Reduction Resulting from Lapse of Applicable Statute of Limitations
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsReductionsResulti.d: Amount of decrease in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from lapses of applicable statutes of limitations.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsDecreasesResultin.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Decrease Resulting from Prior Period Tax Positions
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsDecreasesResultin.d: Amount of decrease in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from tax positions taken in prior period tax returns.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsDecreasesResultin.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Decrease Resulting from Settlements with Taxing Authorities
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsDecreasesResultin.d: Amount of decrease in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from settlements with taxing authorities.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsPeriodIncreaseDec.d: Amount of increase (decrease) in unrecognized tax benefits attributable to uncertain tax positions taken in tax returns.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultin.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Increase Resulting from Current Period Tax Positions
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultin.d: Amount of increase in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from tax positions that have been or will be taken in current period tax return.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultin.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Increase Resulting from Prior Period Tax Positions
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultin.d: Amount of increase in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from tax positions taken in prior period tax returns.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultin.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits, Increase Resulting from Settlements with Taxing Authorities
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultin.d: Amount of increase in unrecognized tax benefits resulting from settlements with taxing authorities.

UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsThatWouldImpactEf.l: Unrecognized Tax Benefits that Would Impact Effective Tax Rate
UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsThatWouldImpactEf.d: The total amount of unrecognized tax benefits that, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation [Table]
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Disclosure of information about unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation arrangement to purchase product and service. Includes, but is not limited to, information about asset pledged to secure payment and payment due in each of next five years and thereafter.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, to be Paid, Year Five
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Amount of fixed and determinable portion of unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation to be paid in fifth fiscal year following current fiscal year. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach). Includes, but is not limited to, lease not yet commenced.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, to be Paid, Year Four
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Amount of fixed and determinable portion of unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation to be paid in fourth fiscal year following current fiscal year. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach). Includes, but is not limited to, lease not yet commenced.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, to be Paid, Year Two
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Amount of fixed and determinable portion of unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation to be paid in second fiscal year following current fiscal year. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach). Includes, but is not limited to, lease not yet commenced.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, to be Paid, Year Three
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Amount of fixed and determinable portion of unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation to be paid in third fiscal year following current fiscal year. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach). Includes, but is not limited to, lease not yet commenced.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, to be Paid, Year One
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Amount of fixed and determinable portion of unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation to be paid in next fiscal year following current fiscal year. Excludes interim and annual periods when interim periods are reported from current statement of financial position date (rolling approach). Includes, but is not limited to, lease not yet commenced.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, Imputed Interest
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: If disclosed, the amount of imputed interest necessary to reduce an unconditional purchase obligation to present value on an unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation.

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, Purchases
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: The amount purchased during the period under an unrecorded unconditional purchase obligation (for example, under the take-or-pay or throughput contract).

UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.l: Unrecorded Unconditional Purchase Obligation, Nature of Variable Components
UnrecordedUnconditionalPurchaseObligatio.d: Description of reasons for changes in the amount of payments under a contractual obligation.

UnrecoveredCostsForPurchasedGasAmount.l: Unrecovered Costs for Purchased Gas Amount
UnrecoveredCostsForPurchasedGasAmount.d: Discloses the amount of unrecovered costs for purchased gas.

UnrecoveredProductionCostsExcessOfEstima.l: Unrecovered Production Costs, Excess of Estimated Average Unit Cost
UnrecoveredProductionCostsExcessOfEstima.d: The aggregate amount of manufacturing or production costs and any related deferred costs (for example, initial tooling costs) that exceeds the aggregate estimated cost of all in-process and delivered units on the basis of the estimated average cost of all units expected to be produced under long-term contracts and programs not yet complete.

UnrecoveredProductionCostsExcessUnrecove.l: Unrecovered Production Costs, Excess Unrecoverable under Existing Firm Orders
UnrecoveredProductionCostsExcessUnrecove.d: The portion of the aggregate amount of manufacturing or production costs and any related deferred costs (for example, initial tooling costs) that exceeds the aggregate estimated cost of all in-process and delivered units on the basis of the estimated average cost of all units expected to be produced under long-term contracts and programs not yet complete, which would not be absorbed in cost of sales based on existing firm orders at the latest balance sheet date.

UnregulatedOperatingRevenue.d: The amount of unregulated operating revenues recognized during the period.

UnregulatedOperationMember.d: Operation of entity not regulated by governmental or other regulatory organizations.

UnremittedEarningsInForeignInvestmentPol.l: Unremitted Earnings in Foreign Investment, Policy [Policy Text Block]
UnremittedEarningsInForeignInvestmentPol.d: Disclosure of accounting policy for tax treatment of unremitted earnings in a foreign investment.

UnsecuredDebtCurrent.d: Carrying value as of the balance sheet date of the portion of long-term, uncollateralized debt obligations due within one year or the normal operating cycle, if longer.

UnsecuredDebtMember.d: Debt obligation not collateralized by pledge of, mortgage of or other lien on the entity's assets.

UnsecuredDebt.d: Including the current and noncurrent portions, carrying value as of the balance sheet date of uncollateralized debt obligations (with maturities initially due after one year or beyond the operating cycle if longer).

UnsecuredLongTermDebt.d: Carrying value as of the balance sheet date of uncollateralized debt obligation (with maturities initially due after one year or beyond the operating cycle if longer), excluding current portion.

UnsolicitedTenderOfferCosts.d: Costs incurred in connection with an unsolicited tender offer (one where the Entity being sought has not requested the offer). These would include costs relating to evaluation and dissemination of information regarding an unsolicited tender offer. A tender offer is a broad solicitation by an Entity or a third party to purchase a substantial percentage of another entity's shares or units for a limited period of time. The offer is at a fixed price, usually at a premium over the current market pric

UnusedLinesOfCreditMember.d: The unused portion of a line of credit that is available to the borrower to withdrawn upon.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemAxis.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both [Axis]
UnusualOrInfrequentItemAxis.d: Information by an event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemDomain.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both [Domain]
UnusualOrInfrequentItemDomain.d: Event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemLineItems.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both [Line Items]
UnusualOrInfrequentItemLineItems.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemTable.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both [Table]
UnusualOrInfrequentItemTable.d: Disclosure of information about the nature and financial statement effect of an event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemNetOfInsurancePro.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both, Net of Insurance Proceeds
UnusualOrInfrequentItemNetOfInsurancePro.d: Amount, after deduction of insurance proceeds, of loss recognized in the income statement for an event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemInsuranceProceeds.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both, Insurance Proceeds
UnusualOrInfrequentItemInsuranceProceeds.d: Amount of insurance proceeds for an event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemNatureOfEventOrTr.l: Unusual or Infrequent Item, or Both, Nature of Event or Transaction
UnusualOrInfrequentItemNatureOfEventOrTr.d: Description of the nature of an event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualOrInfrequentItemsDisclosureTextBl.l: Unusual or Infrequent Items, or Both, Disclosure [Text Block]
UnusualOrInfrequentItemsDisclosureTextBl.d: The entire disclosure for an event or transaction that is unusual in nature or infrequent in occurrence, or both.

UnusualRiskOrUncertaintyImpact.d: Describes the potential impact of the occurrence of the defined risk or adverse resolution of an uncertainty on the entity's financial statements, including a range of potential loss if reasonably estimable.

UnusualRiskOrUncertaintyNatureDomain.d: Describes the nature of the unusual risk or uncertainty, such as the threat of expropriation of its assets by a foreign government, rapid technological obsolescence in the industry, risk of natural disaster from earthquake or weather events, and availability of or continuation of a labor force at a reasonable cost.

UnusualRiskOrUncertaintyByNatureAxis.d: Information by nature of risk and uncertainty, for example, but not limited to, threat of expropriation of its assets by a foreign government, rapid technological obsolescence in the industry, risk of natural disaster from earthquake or weather events, and availability of or continuation of a labor force at a reasonable cost.

UnusualRiskOrUncertaintyLineItems.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

UnusualRiskOrUncertaintyTable.d: Disclosure of information about unusual risk or uncertainty or both and their financial impact or potential financial impact.

UpFrontPaymentArrangementMember.d: Category of deferred revenue by arrangement wherein all amount due is received from customer before delivery of goods or services, and revenue will be recognized upon customer acceptance of delivered goods or services.

UpstreamEquipmentMember.d: Equipment used in the search, development, extraction, and production of natural resources.

PaymentsForOperatingActivities.d: Total amount of cash paid for operating activities during the current period.

UtilitiesOperatingExpense.d: Amount of operating expense of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseDepreciationAnd.l: Utilities Operating Expense, Depreciation and Amortization
UtilitiesOperatingExpenseDepreciationAnd.d: Amount of operating expense for depreciation and amortization of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseGasAndPetroleum.l: Utilities Operating Expense, Gas and Petroleum Purchased
UtilitiesOperatingExpenseGasAndPetroleum.d: Amount of operating expense for purchased gas and petroleum of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseImpairments.d: Amount of operating expense for impairments of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseMaintenance.d: Amount of operating expense for routine plant maintenance and repairs of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseMaintenanceAndO.l: Utilities Operating Expense, Maintenance and Operations
UtilitiesOperatingExpenseMaintenanceAndO.d: Amount of operating expense for routine plant maintenance, repairs and operations of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseOperations.d: Amount of operating expense for routine operations of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseOther.d: Amount of other operating expense of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseProductsAndServ.l: Utilities Operating Expense, Products and Services
UtilitiesOperatingExpenseProductsAndServ.d: Amount of operating expense for products and services of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpensePurchasedPower.d: Amount of operating expense for purchased power of regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpensePurchasedPowerU.l: Utilities Operating Expense, Purchased Power under Long-Term Contracts
UtilitiesOperatingExpensePurchasedPowerU.d: Amount of operating expense for purchased power procured under arrangements extending beyond one year or the normal operating cycle, if longer, by regulated operation.

UtilitiesOperatingExpenseTaxes.d: Amount of operating expense for taxes other than income taxes of regulated operation.

PublicUtilitiesPropertyPlantAndEquipment.l: Public Utilities, Property, Plant and Equipment, Amount of Indirect Disallowance of Costs of Recently Completed Plants
PublicUtilitiesPropertyPlantAndEquipment.d: The amount of indirect disallowance of costs of a recently completed plant. When it becomes probable that part of the cost of a recently completed plant will be disallowed for rate-making purposes and a reasonable estimate of the amount of the disallowance can be made, the estimated amount of the probable disallowance is deducted from the reported cost of the plant and recognized as a loss. If part of the cost is explicitly, but indirectly, disallowed (for example, by an explicit disallowance of

PublicUtilitiesInventory.d: The period end amount for a type of inventory held by the utility in a schedule of inventories.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryTypeDomain.d: Tangible personal property that is held for sale in the ordinary course of business, in process of production for such sale or is to be currently consumed in the production of goods or services to be available for sale.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryAxis.d: Information by type of inventory held.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryCoalMember.d: Combustible mineral substance consisting of carbonized vegetable matter used as fuel and in production of coal gas, water gas, and coal-tar compound.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryFuelMember.d: Any material consumed to produce energy.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryLineItems.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryNaturalGasMember.d: Mixture of gases, liquefied or otherwise, used for fuel and manufacturing purposes, which is ready for sale.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryPetroleumProduct.d: Products obtained from natural gas and oil.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryPropaneMember.d: Heavy, colorless, gaseous alkane occurring naturally in petroleum and natural gas.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryRawMaterialsMemb.d: Basic goods that are to be consumed directly or indirectly in the production of finished goods or services.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryReplacementParts.d: Parts of machinery or equipment held for the purpose of replacing similar parts in the course of repair or maintenance.

PublicUtilitiesInventorySuppliesMember.d: Materials used as supplies by the entity.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryTable.d: Disclosure of information about inventory held by regulated operation entity by type.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryTubularGoodsMemb.d: Pipe and tube products used in the exploration and development of energy resources. Examples include, but are not limited to, drill pipe, pipe casings and oil pipes.

PublicUtilitiesInventoryWaterMember.d: Clear, colorless, odorless and tasteless liquid essential for most plant and animal life comprised of two parts hydrogen and one part oxygen (H2O).

UtilityPlantDomain.d: Plant owned by a utility entity used in the operations of the entity.

VeteransAdministrationLoanMember.d: A loan guaranteed up to certain limits by the Veterans Administration on a principal residence.

VariableInterestEntityReasonForUnavailab.l: Variable Interest Entity, Unavailability of Information, Reasons
VariableInterestEntityReasonForUnavailab.d: Description of the reason that the reporting entity, after making an exhaustive effort, is unable to obtain the information necessary to (1) determine whether the legal entity is a VIE, (2) determine whether it (the reporting entity) is the VIE's primary beneficiary, or (3) perform the accounting required to consolidate the VIE for which it is determined that it (the reporting entity) is the primary beneficiary.

DeferredTaxAssetDomain.d: Identification of the deferred tax asset for which a valuation reserve exists.

ValuationAllowanceByDeferredTaxAssetAxis.l: Valuation Allowance by Deferred Tax Asset [Axis]
ValuationAllowanceByDeferredTaxAssetAxis.d: Information by type of deferred tax consequences attributable to deductible temporary differences.

ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.l: Valuation Allowance for Impairment of Recognized Servicing Assets, Balance
ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.d: Reflects the estimated amount of impairment as of the balance sheet date of recognized servicing assets that are being amortized in proportion to and over the period of estimated net servicing income or loss.

ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.l: Valuation Allowance for Impairment of Recognized Servicing Assets, Period Increase (Decrease)
ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.d: The net increase (decrease) in the valuation allowance for servicing assets subsequently measured using the amortization method.

ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.l: Valuation Allowance for Impairment of Recognized Servicing Assets, Additions (Deductions) for Expenses (Recoveries)
ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.d: Amount of increase (decrease) in the valuation allowance for impairment of contract to service financial assets under which the benefits of servicing are expected to more than adequately compensate the servicer from expenses (recoveries) recognized.

ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.l: Valuation Allowance for Impairment of Recognized Servicing Assets, Sales and Disposals
ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.d: Reduction in valuation allowance of servicing assets based on sales and disposals.

ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.l: Valuation Allowance for Impairment of Recognized Servicing Assets [Line Items]
ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.l: Servicing Asset, Impairment, Valuation Allowance, Activity [Table]
ValuationAllowanceForImpairmentOfRecogni.d: Disclosure of information about activity for valuation allowance from impairment of recognized servicing asset.

ValuationAllowanceLineItems.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

ValuationAllowanceOfDeferredTaxAssetsMem.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowance, Deferred Tax Asset [Member]
ValuationAllowanceOfDeferredTaxAssetsMem.d: Valuation allowance of deferred tax asset attributable to deductible temporary difference and carryforward.

ValuationAllowanceMethodologiesAndAssump.d: Describes the methodologies and assumptions on which the valuation allowance is based for deferred tax assets for which it is more likely than not that all or a portion of the deferred tax asset will not be realized.

ValuationAllowanceTable.d: Disclosure of information about valuation allowance representing portion of deferred tax asset for which it is more likely than not that tax benefit will not be realized.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesAdjustment.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Increase (Decrease) Adjustment
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesAdjustment.d: Amount of increase (decrease) in valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves from adjustment.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesBalance.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Amount
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesBalance.d: Amount of valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesChargedToC.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Additions, Charge to Cost and Expense
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesChargedToC.d: Amount of increase in valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves from charge to cost and expense.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesChargedToO.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Additions, Charge to Other Account
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesChargedToO.d: Amount of increase in valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves from charge to accounts other than cost and expense.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesDeductions.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Deduction
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesDeductions.d: Amount of decrease in valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesRecoveries.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Addition, Recovery
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesRecoveries.d: Amount of increase in valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves from recovery of amount previously written off or reestablishment of reserve previously utilized.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesReservesOf.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves, Business Acquired
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesReservesOf.d: Amount of increase in valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves from business combination.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesDomain.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves [Domain]
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesDomain.d: Valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves.

ValuationAllowancesAndReservesTypeAxis.l: SEC Schedule, 12-09, Valuation Allowances and Reserves Type [Axis]
ValuationAllowancesAndReservesTypeAxis.d: Information by valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves.

ValueAddedTaxReceivable.d: Carrying amount as of the balance sheet date of value added taxes due either from customers arising from sales on credit terms, or as previously overpaid to tax authorities.

ValueOfBusinessAcquiredVOBA.l: Present Value of Future Insurance Profits, Net
ValueOfBusinessAcquiredVOBA.d: Amount, after accumulated amortization, of present value of future profits of insurance contract acquired in business combination.

VariableAnnuityMember.d: Contract providing periodic payment that varies according to investment experience of separate account in which amount paid to provide for annuity is allocated.

ScheduleOfVariableInterestEntitiesTable.d: Disclosure of information about variable interest held, whether or not such variable interest entity (VIE) is included in consolidated financial statements.

VariableInterestEntityLineItems.d: Line items represent financial concepts included in a table. These concepts are used to disclose reportable information associated with domain members defined in one or many axes to the table.

VariableInterestEntityNotPrimaryBenefici.d: Variable Interest Entities (VIE) in which the entity does not have a controlling financial interest (as defined) and of which it is therefore not the primary beneficiary.
